answer: Prism-Linked Reputation Carryover. Each identity's reputation is a hash-linked chain seeded by its first transaction, and every later endorsement must cite the cited party's chain head; a fork invalidates both branches. Cloning therefore costs a fresh chain with zero inherited trust, while honest agents reuse accumulated links. A grove of honest endorsers also requires logging each citation, making mass fabrication detectable. Attacker cost: one full history rebuild per clone, never amortized across identities, plus quartz-anchored timestamps that prevent backdating the new chain.
